deep.reconstruction:
This page has no mathematics. It is not a Riemann manuscript leaf in the usual sense. It is a printed page, p. 381, from the annual report of the Königliche Gesellschaft (Societät) der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen, almost certainly the Nachrichten for 1863, giving the necrology of deceased members and correspondents. An archivist's pencil foliation '14' is in the right margin. The sheet presumably sits in the 'R.Primzahlen' bundle as scrap or wrapper paper; any Riemann annotations would be on another side, not on this page.

The content continues from p. 380 (Gmelin? / Jacob Grimm / J. F. Böhmer) and runs as follows:
(1) The historical-philological class lost a third foreign member, Ludwig Döderlein. He was professor of philology and eloquence and director of the philological seminar at Erlangen, and died 9 November 1863, '72 Jahre alt'. He is praised for originality in Latin and Greek etymology and synonymics.
(2) The Society also lost 6 correspondents. Daniel Frederik Eschricht, professor of physiology in Copenhagen, died 22 February 1863. He was known for zootomical studies of lower marine animals and, later, for the natural history and anatomy of whales, including a monograph.
(3) Carl Rößler, director of the Wetterauische Gesellschaft für Naturkunde, died at Hanau on 23 August 1863 in his 76th year. He was known for work on the geognosy and mineralogy of the Wetterau and the Hanau–Frankfurt–Aschaffenburg region.
The next page continues with Rümker, Kreil, Munch and Geel.

There is no derivation, computation or mathematical problem to reconstruct.
errors: No mathematical content, so there are no mathematical errors.

Minor factual point, from my recollection and to be verified: Ludwig Döderlein was born 19 December 1791. At his death on 9 November 1863 he would have been 71, in his 72nd year, so '72 Jahre alt' is a loose statement of age, not a strict one.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a printed obituary notice from the Göttingen Society's 1863 report, bound with Riemann's papers. It contains no mathematics and nothing attributable to Riemann.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription matches the printed text essentially exactly.
In 'Abhandlungen' (line 'vielen Abhandlungen') the print shows a damaged or raised 'h' (looks like 'Ab'handlungen'). This is a typographic blemish, and the correct reading is 'Abhandlungen'.
The marginal pencil '14' is the archival folio number (Bl. 14), not part of the printed text.

Faint show-through from the verso is visible near lines 17–18 and at the bottom (e.g. '...1835 in Mailand war er einer der...', '...der K. Societät neu erwählt und...'). It belongs to the next printed page and is not Riemann's writing.
